evidence: Full CDIAL danta explicitly gives regional dā̃t tooth across Nepali, Bihari, Hindi and western IA, alongside dand and the proposed Nepali dā̃d stage. The selected dãṭ/ḍãṭ/ḍaṭ/ḍãt/dath and Dotyali dā̃dā tooth responses fit this family with source dental/retroflex notation, nasalization, aspiration spelling and final vowel retained. Local IA transmission is unresolved. The separate non-nasal Dotyali dāḍā and longer compound/extended tooth forms are excluded for separate review.

Full CDIAL nasta subsection 1 explicitly gives Torwali natkōl nose and Maiyan nathūr nose. Torwali netkel and Mai nasūr/nāsūr are provisionally grouped with those exact regional comparisons, preserving source vowels and s versus th notation. Turner marks the extension of natkōl and related forms with uncertainty; no independent origin of the whole extension or component segmentation is asserted. Regional transmission remains unresolved. This uses the nose-bearing branch, not the separate nastā nose-ring branch.
